The main jump occurs from $K{=}1$ to $K{=}5$ (+5.7\,pp), while $K{=}5$ to $K{=}10$ adds +0.8\,pp and $K{=}10$ to $K{=}20$ adds +2.2\,pp, supporting the adaptive allocation strategy over fixed high-$K$.
At $K{=}1$, CRM correction alone falls below the VLA-only baseline (10.3\% vs.\ $11.0$\%), because the single sample lacks argmin centering and shifts outside the CRM's training distribution. Multi-sample selection is an enabling condition for effective correction.
The diminishing-returns pattern is loosely analogous to inference-time compute scaling in LLMs~\cite{snell2024scaling}, though the mechanism differs: in our setting, additional samples improve the starting point for correction rather than enabling better selection.
$K{=}5$ captures ${\sim}$85\% of the $K{=}10$ benefit at half the compute cost, suggesting a practical operating point when compute budget is constrained.
